questions.prompt: What does a red octagonal sign indicate?
questions.explanation: A red octagonal sign indicates a stop sign, requiring drivers to come to a complete stop.
A speed limit is the maximum speed allowed when conditions are good. In rain, snow, fog or heavy traffic, drive slower than the posted limit.

choices.text: The speed you should travel under all driving conditions
The minimum speed permitted on all highways
The maximum speed permitted when conditions are favourable
The maximum speed permitted except when passing

questions.explanation: The white X-shaped crossbuck marks a railway crossing. Slow down, look and listen in both directions, and be ready to stop for a train.
A bent arrow on a yellow diamond warns of a curve ahead in the direction the arrow points. Slow down before you reach the curve.
This warning sign tells you a yield sign is ahead. Slow down and be prepared to yield the right-of-way.
This orange triangle with a red border is displayed on the back of vehicles that normally travel slower than 40 km/h, such as farm equipment. Be ready to slow down, and pass only when it is safe.

choices.text: Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic
Dangerous goods vehicle placard: flammable gas

questions.explanation: A wavy arrow warns of a series of curves ahead. Slow down and stay in your lane.
This sign warns of a school bus stop ahead. Watch for a stopped bus and for children, and be ready to stop when its red lights flash.
The fluorescent yellow-green diamond with two children warns of a school crosswalk ahead. Slow down and watch for children crossing.
This sign tells you the road carries traffic in both directions, for example where a one-way section ends. Keep to the right.
Traffic will merge into your lane from the side shown. Be ready to adjust your speed or change lanes to let vehicles in.
A white diamond on a black background marks a reserved lane. Only the vehicles shown (here, buses and taxis) may use it, during the times shown.

choices.text: Lane is reserved for use by the specified vehicles
Lane can be used for dangerous goods vehicles

questions.explanation: The left edge of the road moves in ahead, so the road becomes narrower. Slow down and be ready to move right.
This sign warns of a bump or rough section of road ahead. Slow down to keep control of your vehicle.
A walking figure on a yellow diamond warns of a pedestrian crosswalk ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop for pedestrians.
A red circle and slash over two cars means passing is not allowed. Stay in your lane until a sign or road markings show passing is permitted again.
A yellow-and-black checkerboard marks the end of the road. Slow down and be ready to stop or turn around.
This sign warns that the road ahead becomes divided by a median. Keep to the right of the median.
A white H on a square service sign shows the way to a hospital.
Orange signs mark construction zones. This one warns of people working ahead: slow down, obey the posted speed limit, and watch for workers. Fines double when workers are present.

questions.prompt: At 9:00 AM on a school day, what is the maximum speed permitted in a school zone in a rural area, unless otherwise posted?
questions.explanation: Unless otherwise posted, the school zone speed limit is 30 km/h during school zone hours on school days. This applies in rural areas as well as in towns and cities.

questions.prompt: Parking in a space reserved for persons with disabilities is permitted:
questions.explanation: Spaces reserved for persons with disabilities may only be used by vehicles that display a valid disabled parking placard or licence plate.

choices.text: While the driver is waiting in the vehicle
When the vehicle has a proper identifying placard or license plate
When all other parking spaces are filled
When a driver stops for less than 5 minutes

questions.prompt: The speed limit in a construction zone must be obeyed:
questions.explanation: A posted construction zone speed limit applies whenever the signs are up, whether or not you can see workers. Speeding fines double when workers are present.

choices.text: Only when a flag person is posted nearby
Only when construction workers are present

questions.prompt: Unless otherwise posted, the school zone speed limits are in effect on school days during the following hours:
questions.explanation: Unless signs show otherwise, school zone limits apply on school days from 8:00 to 9:30 am, 11:30 am to 1:30 pm, and 3:00 to 4:30 pm.

choices.text: 8:30 am to 9:30 am, 12:00 pm to 1:00 pm and 3:30 pm to 4:00 pm
8:00 am to 9:30 am, 11:30 am to 1:30 pm and 3:00 pm to 4:30 pm

questions.prompt: A "slow moving vehicle" sign must be displayed on the rear of any vehicle that normally travels at speeds less than:
questions.explanation: Farm machinery, construction equipment and other vehicles that normally travel slower than 40 km/h must display the orange-and-red slow moving vehicle triangle on the rear. Key words: "slow moving vehicle", "speeds less".

questions.prompt: Unless otherwise posted, what is the basic speed limit outside a city, town or village on a primary highway?
questions.explanation: 100 km/h is the maximum speed limit on a provincial highway located outside an urban area in Alberta. (Refer to Driver's guide for car and light truck. Chap 2. p 27)
A green circle on a white sign means the action shown is permitted. This one, with a black diamond, marks a route that vehicles carrying dangerous goods may use. (Driver's Guide p. 29)
A red WRONG WAY sign means you are travelling against oncoming traffic. Stop and turn around safely. (Driver's Guide p. 26)

choices.text: You are going the wrong way into oncoming traffic

questions.explanation: A white bar on a red circle means do not enter. It is often posted at the exit end of one-way roads and ramps. (Driver's Guide p. 26)
A white arrow on a black rectangle means traffic may only travel in the direction of the arrow. (Driver's Guide p. 27)

choices.text: Proceed in the direction of the arrow only

questions.explanation: This sign is placed before a median or traffic island. Keep to the right of the divider. (Driver's Guide p. 27)
A green circle on a white square means the action shown is permitted. Here, traffic must turn left. (Driver's Guide p. 29)

choices.text: Left turn on green arrow only

questions.explanation: A green circle around two vehicles means passing is permitted. Pass only when it is safe. (Driver's Guide p. 29)
A red circle and slash means the action inside is not permitted. This sign prohibits left turns. (Driver's Guide p. 29)
A red circle and slash over a right arrow means right turns are not permitted at this location. (Driver's Guide p. 29)

choices.text: No right turn on red only

questions.explanation: A red circle and slash over a U-shaped arrow means U-turns are not permitted. (Driver's Guide p. 29)

choices.text: Turn around at the end of the road

questions.explanation: This prohibitive sign means you must not pass cyclists on this section of road. (Driver's Guide p. 29)
A red circle and slash over a truck means trucks are not permitted on this road. (Driver's Guide p. 30)

choices.text: Steep hill, trucks use low gear

questions.explanation: A red circle and slash over a black diamond means vehicles carrying dangerous goods are not permitted. A green circle with the diamond marks a dangerous goods route. (Driver's Guide pp. 29–30)
A red circle and slash over a P means parking is not permitted. An arrow under the symbol shows where the rule applies. (Driver's Guide p. 30)

choices.text: Parking for persons with disabilities only

questions.explanation: A red circle and slash over a stop-sign shape means stopping is not permitted, not even briefly to drop off passengers. (Driver's Guide p. 30)

questions.prompt: You see this sign with no speed limit sign attached to it. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: A school sign without a speed sign marks a school area. Children may be walking or crossing, so use caution. With a speed sign attached, it is a school zone. (Driver's Guide p. 31)

choices.text: A school area: use caution, as children may be walking or crossing
A school zone: the speed limit is 30 km/h
A school crosswalk: you must stop

questions.prompt: This sign has a 30 km/h speed sign attached. When is the 30 km/h limit in effect, unless other times are posted?
questions.explanation: This is a school zone. Unless other times are posted, it is in effect on school days from 8:00 to 9:30 a.m., 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m., and 3:00 to 4:30 p.m. (Driver's Guide p. 30)

choices.text: Every day from 8:30 a.m. to one hour after sunset
At all times, every day of the year

questions.prompt: This sign has a speed sign attached. When is the playground zone speed limit in effect, unless other times are posted?
questions.explanation: Playground zone restrictions are in effect every day from 8:30 a.m. to one hour after sunset, unless other times are posted. (Driver's Guide p. 31)

choices.text: On school days only, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
Every day from 8:30 a.m. to one hour after sunset

questions.prompt: May you pass another vehicle travelling in the same direction in a zone marked by this sign and a speed limit sign, while the zone is in effect?
questions.explanation: You must not pass or attempt to pass another vehicle travelling in the same direction within a playground zone when the speed restriction is in effect. The same rule applies in school zones. (Driver's Guide p. 31)

choices.text: Yes, if the vehicle ahead is going below 30 km/h
Yes, if no children are visible

questions.explanation: This warning sign tells you a stop sign is ahead, often where it is hidden by a curve or hill. Be ready to stop. (Driver's Guide p. 33)
This warning sign tells you there are traffic control signals ahead. (Driver's Guide p. 33)

questions.prompt: The yellow lights on this sign are flashing. What should you do?
questions.explanation: When the yellow lights flash, prepare to stop: the traffic signal ahead is turning from green to yellow or yellow to red, or is already red. (Driver's Guide p. 33)

choices.text: Prepare to stop, because the signal ahead is changing or is red
Speed up to get through before the light changes
Proceed with caution; the signal ahead is flashing yellow
Stop at the sign, then proceed

questions.explanation: A right-angle arrow warns of a sharp turn to the right. A bent, curved arrow means a gentler curve. Slow down before the turn. (Driver's Guide p. 33)
This sign warns that animals such as deer often cross here. Watch the ditches, especially at dusk and dawn. (Driver's Guide pp. 34, 84)
A bicycle on a yellow diamond warns that cyclists may cross the road ahead. (Driver's Guide p. 34)
This sign warns that motorized snow vehicles (snowmobiles) may cross the road ahead. (Driver's Guide p. 34)
This sign warns of a side road (which may be hidden) joining from the right. Watch for vehicles entering. (Driver's Guide p. 34)

choices.text: Side road on the right ahead

questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead splits into a Y intersection. (Driver's Guide p. 34)
This sign warns that the road ends at a T intersection. You will have to turn left or right. (Driver's Guide p. 34)
This sign warns of a roundabout ahead. Slow down, yield to traffic already in the roundabout, and travel counterclockwise. (Driver's Guide pp. 34, 61)
This sign warns that trucks may enter the road from the right. Be ready to slow down. (Driver's Guide p. 34)
Roads join side-by-side but do not merge: the entering traffic gets its own lane (free flow). Neither lane needs to merge. (Driver's Guide p. 34)

choices.text: Added lane (free flow): traffic enters its own lane

questions.explanation: The right lane ends ahead. Drivers in it must merge left when it is safe, and drivers in the left lane should let them in. (Driver's Guide p. 35)
Both edges of the road move in ahead, so the road becomes narrower on both sides. (Driver's Guide p. 35)
This sign warns of a narrow passage, such as a narrow bridge, that may be only wide enough for one vehicle. (Driver's Guide p. 35)
The median ends ahead and traffic will travel in both directions on an undivided road. Keep right. (Driver's Guide p. 35)
This sign warns of a steep hill. Check your speed, and with a manual transmission, shift to a lower gear to avoid overheating the brakes. (Driver's Guide pp. 35, 76)
The paved surface ends ahead and the road continues as gravel or dirt. Slow down before you reach it. (Driver's Guide p. 35)
This sign warns of rumble strips ahead: grooves in the pavement that make noise and vibration to alert drivers. (Driver's Guide p. 35)
A chevron sign marks a sharp bend in the road and points in the direction of the turn. (Driver's Guide p. 35)

choices.text: A sharp bend in the direction shown

questions.explanation: This sign warns that cyclists may use the full lane ahead, and the lane is too narrow for a vehicle and bicycle to travel side by side. (Driver's Guide p. 35)

choices.text: Cyclists may use the full lane, which is too narrow to share side by side

questions.explanation: This orange construction sign warns of a flag person ahead. Obey the flag person's signals and be ready to stop. (Driver's Guide p. 37)
This orange construction sign warns that a survey crew is working ahead. Slow down and watch for workers. (Driver's Guide p. 37)

questions.prompt: What shape and colour is a sign that marks a school zone or school area?
questions.explanation: School zone and school area signs are pentagon-shaped with a fluorescent yellow-green background. (Driver's Guide p. 25)

questions.prompt: What colour background do signs giving construction area information have?
questions.explanation: Construction signs show information or pictures on an orange background, in a diamond shape. (Driver's Guide p. 25)

questions.prompt: Signs on a blue background usually show:
questions.explanation: White messages on blue square signs show places for fuel, food, lodging, or assistance. Green signs give distances and destinations. (Driver's Guide p. 26)

choices.text: Services such as fuel, food, lodging, or assistance
